units.title: Landscape Design Process
units.topics: Understanding the process of Landscape Design its stages, Site analysis and site planning, use of landscape elements in the design of outdoor spaces , visual and experiential quality of designed landscapes

units.title: Nature
units.topics: a) Botany, Plant systematics: Introduction to and fundamentals of botany and plant systematics , their relevance to Landscape Architecture Practice. b) Geology, Geomorphology and Soil Sciences: Introduction to and fundamentals of Geology, Geomorphology and Soil Sciences , their relevance to Landscape Architecture Practice. c) Hydrology: Introduction to and fundamentals of hydrology and their relevance to Landscape Architecture Practice

units.title: Ecosystems
units.topics: Fundamentals of ecology, natural cycles, life cycle analysis, Introduction to natural Ecosystems and biomes in India with focus on Sahyadri ranges and other ecosystems in Maharashtra region

units.title: Climatology
units.topics: Fundamentals of climatology, Introduction to climatic zones, climatic comfort, climatic analysis, role of a landscape architect in mitigating climate change and modifying microclimate at micro and macro scales, introduction to software related to climatological analysis for a landscape architecture project

subjects.title: Theory and Readings in Landscape Architecture -1

units.title: Landscape Architecture Theory and Reading
units.topics: Understanding the need & scope of theory and the tools to study with respect to landscape architecture, importance of reading and taking notes from literature

units.title: Man- nature relationship
units.topics: Changing perceptions of man’s relationship with nature from ancient times, human beings living in natural forests, human responses to nature and landscape resources as a function of this perception, ancient Indian landscapes, theory of cultural landscape, cultural landscapes of India, concept of global and local, concept of human centric vs nature centric responses to the environment

units.title: Theories in and relevant to the field of landscape architecture
units.topics: Concept of Entropy, Concept of indigenous and non-indigenous contexts, Savana hypothesis, Prospect- refuge theory, Defensible space, Introduction to landscape design theory, systems thinking theory etc., and their possible applications in the contemporary landscape design/planning

units.title: Introduction to Landscape Representation
units.topics: Role and need of representation in landscape design, styles of representation based on purpose and scales of landscapes (site, neighbourhood, urban, regional, etc.).

units.title: Reading and drawing maps
units.topics: reading maps of various types and scales, learning to understand and draw graphic scale, north etc., understanding theme maps with legends and symbols

units.title: Landscape Representation tools and techniques
units.topics: Freehand sketching for quick graphic communication, rendering, drawings plans, sections, elevations and views, using various mediums, various techniques of drawing landscapes, drawing tools (manual and digital), understanding the basics of diagramming and infographics and composition of the graphics for a portfolio/ panel/sheet/ presentation poster, etc.

units.title: Mapping and analysis
units.topics: Site/study area visits, mapping and detail landscape analysis of macro and micro setting, Introduction to legends and titles of maps landscape elements/features, creating various theme maps, resources mapping, landscape character analysis, synthesis and suitability explorations through theme maps and other graphical representations

units.title: Landscape Architecture project formulation and the outcome
units.topics: Formulation of the project brief with scope and suitable approach and evolving in stages the landscape concept, spatial structure and design/planning solutions, landscape architecture interventions with respect to ecological, functional, cultural & visual context , with basic understanding of rules and regulations and legal frameworks as found relevant for the project

units.title: Project representation
units.topics: Evolving a textual narrative with context-based vocabulary and representing the process through diagramming and other graphical representation techniques learnt in semester-1

units.title: Ecosystem Analysis
units.topics: Principles and techniques of ecosystem analysis and documentation

units.title: Ecological restoration
units.topics: Concept of ecological restoration, introduction to global and local approaches to ecological restoration through case studies based on literature and/or field visits

units.title: Planting
units.topics: Introduction to significance, relevance and designing with plants in natural and designed, indoor and outdoor settings, principles of planting and basis for selection of plants, designing and drawing planting scheme for a selected area/project illustrating the learnings

subjects.title: Theory and Readings in Landscape Architecture-2

units.title: Traditions in Landscape Architecture
units.topics: Studying landscape design approaches, design vocabulary & philosophy through projects/landscapes in the past, starting from the ancient till late 19th century along with insights into natural, social & temporal context, their relevance in the contemporary context, emphasizing on historic landscapes and world natural heritage sites in India and in Maharashtra , works of Geoffrey Jellicoe, Burle Marx, Lawrence Halprin, and other famous landscape architects across the globe, works by Indian landscape architects -Ram Sharma, M.Shaheer, Ravindra Bhan, Kishore Pradhan, etc.

units.title: Landscape planning and spatial open space structure
units.topics: Understanding the evolution of landscape architecture in post-industrial world & the concepts of park, park systems & open space structure. Understanding the development of open space structure in the context of landscape architecture, urban design, and planning context. ( Early industrial town and the garden city movement), Understanding contributions by Frederic Law Olmstead, Patrick Geddes and recognition of landscape architecture as a profession, Examples of open space development in new towns and urban renewal to illustrate the close conceptual relationship between Town Planning, Urban Design and landscape Planning, environmental planning theory by Ian McHarg, theory of landscape aesthetics, theory of biomimicry , landscape urbanism, etc. , Understanding the significance and influence of Ian McHarg on mid and late 20th Century landscape architecture, role played in urban and regional planning projects by landscape architects in India

units.title: Contemporary and Futuristic Landscapes
units.topics: Contemporary (late 19 th C and beyond) landscape projects , futuristic approaches and conceptual understanding for designed landscapes across the world and their changing relationship with nature, studied through relevant case studies, seminars and through readings (sustainable low carbon, resilient, parametric, vertical landscapes, biophilia, virtually immersive landscapes, etc.), Introduction to the concept of AI (Artificial Intelligence) and role of AI (Artificial Intelligence) in shaping of contemporary and future designed landscapes

units.title: Understanding contours, Site Survey and Appraisal
units.topics: Topographic surveys and their methods, visualizing landforms, their graphical representation, deriving contours by method of interpolation , contours and their characteristics, Establishing relationship between site characteristics and design requirements. Process of site analysis / documentation with respect to gradient, slope analysis, relief, aspect, surface water regime , learning from site/field visits, etc.

units.title: Earth form Grading
units.topics: Introduction to understanding landform and its grading design (pathways, roads, parking, mounds, etc.), grading techniques, calculations of earth work

units.title: Storm water systems
units.topics: Introduction to storm water drainage, systems and types, understanding drainage pattern and watershed area, storm water run -off systems and their design, calculation related to the design of storm water system, concept of watershed, ridge-valley lines and water basins, nature-based solutions in storm water management

units.title: Introduction to landscape architecture services and construction
units.topics: Landscape services such as irrigation, storm water drainage, lighting, plumbing, fountains, swimming pools, understanding basics about materials and construction techniques used in designed landscapes , materials and construction techniques

units.title: Introduction to landscape architecture working drawings
units.topics: Basics of landscape architecture working drawing, methods, types, modes, significance of the working drawings, reading working drawings for accurate execution on site, making important working drawings for a landscape design project- process and deliverables
